# send

Sends data.

```ttl
send <data1> <data2>....
```

## Remarks

Causes Tera Term to send characters to the host.
If &lt;data&gt; is a string, the string is sent to the host.
If &lt;data&gt; is an integer, its lowest-order byte (0-255) is regarded as an ASCII code of the character, and the character is sent to the host.

Send characters to VTWin following [local echo setting](https://teratermproject.github.io/manual/5/en/html/menu/setup-additional-terminal.html#localecho).

The data are checked, and when data is judged to be text, data is sent in same as "[sendtext](sendtext.md)"; when data is judged to be binary, data is sent in same as "[sendbinary](sendbinary.md)".

Example send 'ABC' ; Send "ABC". (ASCII code of the character "A" is 65.) send 65 66 67 myname='Tera Term' send 'My name is ' myname '.' ; "ABC" send $41 $42 $43 ; "1" value = $31 send value ; "31" value = $31 sprintf2 command "%02X" value send command /* "CTRL+C" is 3 in binary so just send 3 like so. * * CTRL+A = 1, CTRL+B = 2.................. CTRL+Z = 26. */ send #3 /* Send the tab code. */ send #9

See also "[setsync](setsync.md)" for the synchronous mode.
